caption: A small blowtorch is played over charcoal in a barbecue, and the coals begin to glow where the flame touches them.

sa.check: A blowtorch is played over charcoal in a barbecue.
The coals begin to glow where the flame touches them.
The glow spreads to neighbouring coals.
The flame points where the torch points.
The coals are black before the torch reaches them.
The torch comes first and the glow follows.

pc.expect: The glow appears only where the torch is aimed and spreads from there to the coals beside it.
pc.fail: The coals glow before the torch reaches them; or the torch plays on a coal and it stays black to the end of the clip; or the glow appears on the far side of the bed from the torch; or the whole bed glows at once while the torch plays on one spot.

pc.expect: The glow only spreads and brightens and does not go out where it has caught.
pc.fail: A glowing coal goes black again while the torch plays nearby; or the glow spreads and then retreats; or the glow brightens and dims in turn; or the ash gathers back into black charcoal.

pc.expect: The torch's flame points where it is aimed and any smoke or sparks from the coals rise.
pc.fail: The flame droops downward as the torch is tilted up; or the smoke sinks into the barbecue and pools; or sparks fall through the grate and lie glowing below; or the flame hangs below the nozzle.

pc.expect: The coals stay hard lumps that glow and crust with ash, and the torch stays a rigid tool.
pc.fail: A coal melts or flows under the flame; or the coals swell as they glow; or the torch's nozzle melts; or the ash holds a rigid shape when the coals shift.

pc.expect: One torch and one bed of coals; the coals keep their number and stay in the barbecue.
pc.fail: A coal vanishes leaving no ash; or new coals appear with none added; or a coal passes through the grate and out below; or a second torch appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The barbecue's body, the grate and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The barbecue changes colour; or the grate changes spacing; or items around the barbecue rearrange.
